external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A sensor node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites
external_entities.notes: Nodes are outside the system owner's physical control.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards

external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A customer associated with sensor nodes and the customer data in the telemetry lake.
external_entities.source_excerpt: to find out which customer the node belongs to

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them onward.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that consumes readings and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry containing device information used to check keys and identify the associated customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service onto which the gateway forwards accepted readings.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery telemetry store containing site addresses and occupancy patterns, which are customer data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not say whether firmware images are signed before installation.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes publish readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up the device in the device registry to check the key and identify the customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery
data_flows.data_description: sensor readings including site addresses and occupancy patterns

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes poll the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over a local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: Fleet operators view dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: customer site
trust_boundaries.description: A customer-controlled site where sensor nodes are installed and serviced.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone through which sensor nodes connect and from which the firmware bucket is publicly readable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The analytics network containing the telemetry normalizer and telemetry processing services.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface because it is an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the device gateway as an MQTT broker.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer presents a non-web interface because it is a Python consumer.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies it as a Python consumer rather than a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is grouped in the analytics network because the source gives no separate network zone for it.
assumptions.basis: The registry is a cloud data store used by the gateway, and no distinct zone is stated; it is assigned to the named analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is grouped in the analytics network because the source gives no separate network zone for it.
assumptions.basis: Pub/Sub carries readings to the telemetry normalizer in the named analytics network, and no distinct zone is stated.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns that the source calls customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the lake contains site addresses and occupancy patterns and is customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is grouped in the analytics network because the source gives no separate storage zone for it.
assumptions.basis: The lake is the destination of the normalizer in the named analytics network, and no distinct zone is stated.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential because it contains device keys and customer associations.
assumptions.basis: The source says the registry is used to check the key and determine which customer the node belongs to.
